Fully ablative CO2 lasers remove the entire surface layer of the treated skin. This provides intensive rejuvenation and is very effective for deep wrinkles, significant sun damage, or scarring. Fractional CO2 lasers, on the other hand, target only portions of the skin in a pixelated pattern, leaving areas of healthy skin between treated zones. Gel padding tends to lose its shape and effectiveness over time, becoming less comfortable on longer or frequent rides. This means you might notice the seat getting less supportive after a while, especially if you ride often or for extended periods.  Regarding gel seat covers, while they add cushioning, some users experience slipping or shifting during rides, which can be uncomfortable and distracting. However, certain gel seat covers address this issue by including features like anti-slip grips, secure drawstrings, or non-slip interiors to help keep the cover firmly in place. For example, some covers feature adjustable straps or a slip-resistant interior specifically designed to prevent movement, even on rough or wet trails.  If you decide to try a gel seat cover, look for one with these anti-slip features and moisture-absorbing materials, which can also help keep you comfortable when biking in rainy weather or on forest trails. This should make your rides smoother and more enjoyable, without the hassle of the cushion slipping.

Gel saddles and gel seat covers are soft and provide a good degree of comfort if you are riding less than an hour and only a few times a week. It is commonly recommended for beginners and casual riders. However, over time the gel will become compacted and lose its springiness which will affect comfort. Gel saddles might be best used for shorter distance rides because you might find they lack the stability and support necessary for trails. In addition, there is no evidence that gel seats help reduce perineal symptoms if those are of concern.

Gel seat covers are made to stay in place. They usually have an interior anti-slip interior fabric, strong drawstrings that tightens the seat cover to the bike saddle,  and side strings to attach the seat cover to the seat pole. However, some experts recommend cyclists wear padded bike shorts rather than using a gel seat cover to achieve the needed cushioning while having maximum flexibility.

response: Given your preference for comfort and past back pain, a gel cushion add-on seat is a suitable choice. When selecting one, consider the following important features:  1. **Pressure Relief Channel**: Many high-quality gel cushions, such as Bikeroo’s, include a pressure relief channel. This feature helps reduce pressure on sensitive areas and can support better posture, which may help with your back pain.  2. **Anti-Slip Surface**: To address your concern about slipping, look for cushions with anti-slip bases or surfaces. This will keep the cushion securely in place during your rides, even on rough forest trails or in rainy weather.  3. **Durability and Support**: Some gel cushions combine gel with durable memory foam for enhanced support and longevity. This combination helps the cushion maintain its shape and comfort over time.  4. **Easy Installation**: Since you prefer not to handle complex DIY tasks, choose a cushion that is easy to install, usually with simple straps or a slip-on design.  5. **Size and Fit**: Make sure the cushion matches the width and shape of your current saddle for optimal comfort and stability.  By focusing on these features, you can enhance your riding comfort and reduce the risk of further back pain.

Your perfect saddle depends on your body and cycling habits. Core strength, posture, where you cycle, your pelvis width, and your bone structure all determine which saddle will be the most comfortable for you. You should make sure the shape of the saddle conforms to your anatomy, that it gives you good balance and does not exert undo pressure or friction on your thighs, perineum, and glutes. The saddle should not be too narrow nor too wide. Extra wide saddles also are available for cyclists that maybe a bit overweight. Although unusual for mountain bikes, since you have had back problems you might consider a kick-up on the back of the saddle that prevents you from sliding while climbing and supports your lower back while pedaling. 

Besides bike saddles, the wheels, the curb front fork and the seat post suspension all play a role in reducing the shock from bumps and can make your bike ride much more comfortable.

Upgrading your bike pedals is a matter of personal preference. There are two main types, flat and clipless pedals.

Flat bike pedals have a series of studs or pins in different positions across both surfaces of the pedal. Pins are adjustable and are placed to optimize your shoe placement. Some pins or studs can be sharp and might pose a hazard. A flat pedal can also fold up, making it convenient for storage and traveling by bus and train. The wide platform of the flat peddle allows you to exert leverage during cornering and pumping hard while adjusting foot placement to gain control over the bike for different terrains. Flat pedals also have either a concave or convex rim shape. The convex shape allows easier slip and adjusting, while the concave shape boosts mud shedding properties.

Clipless pedals are a popular choice for a casual rider for a smoother ride and are great at giving you more power on each stroke.

You should look for a strong pedal with good grip because of the rough terrain and wet weather you will encounter. Pedals are made from  either a nylon composite, that can handle a lot of bashing on rocks before it sees serious wear, or a machined aluminum alloy, steel, or titanium. In general, a metal pedal will last longer than a nylon composite. High end pedals will have a fully sealed bearing so no dust, dirt, or moisture will be able to get in and can be serviced.

response: To determine the perfect chain length, you have a couple of reliable methods:  1. **Largest Cog and Chainring Method**: Shift your bike so the chain is on the largest front chainring and the largest rear cog. With the chain routed through the derailleur, pull it tight. The derailleur should have a slight bend, and the jockey wheels should not be overstretched. If the chain is loose here, it is likely too long. You should remove links until the chain is just long enough to fit this position, plus an additional link or two for safety and smooth shifting.  2. **Matching the Old Chain**: If you still have the old chain and it was the correct length, you can lay the new chain next to it and match the number of links.  After sizing, check by shifting into the smallest chainring and smallest cog. The chain should not be so long that it hangs or sags excessively; the derailleur should still maintain some tension.  Since you often ride in hilly and rough areas and commute with your bike, a properly sized chain is essential for reliable shifting and to prevent the chain from coming off during rides. If you need to remove links, use a chain tool for accuracy.

question: I tried to go on the largest gears of my bike, and I see that the chain seems a bit loose. How to know the perfect length of a chain for a bike?

response: No worries—there is a straightforward method that does not require any complicated math. To find the correct chain length, take your new chain and thread it around the largest front chainring and the largest rear cog, making sure to skip the derailleur entirely. Once the chain is in place, pull the ends together and add one full link (one inner and one outer link). This will give you the correct length for your bike. You can then use your chain tool to cut the chain to this size.   If you would rather avoid the hassle, you might also consider using an online chain length calculator, which can quickly give you the answer by inputting a few simple measurements. You should be able to make the shift to the largest cog easily.  You should also see two slight bends at each jockey wheel of the rear derailleur.  If the chain is too short, this shift is difficult to make, and the derailleur cage is stretched out and almost parallel to the chainstay. A more precise method includes removing your current chain.   Once the chain has been removed, shift the front derailleur to the largest chainring, and the rear to the smallest. Wrap the chain around the largest chainring (at the rear), making that if the chain has an outer plate, it is routed toward the front chainring.  Pass the chain through the front derailleur cage and onto the largest front chainring, Hold chain at the 5 o’clock position. response: I am glad the adjustment worked for you. For lubricating your bike chain, it is best to use lubricants specifically designed for bicycles. Specialized bike chain lubricants are formulated to handle the conditions you often encounter, such as rain, dust, and rough paths, and they help repel dirt and water while minimizing chain wear.  Car engine oil is not recommended, as it is too thick for bike chains. Using it can increase resistance, attract more dirt, and reduce the lifespan of your chain. In emergencies, lighter oils like sewing machine oil can be used, but for regular maintenance, a proper bike chain lube—ideally one with Teflon®—will provide the best performance and longevity, especially given your riding habits in varied weather and on rough terrain.  If you ever run out of bike-specific lube, 90 or 140 grade gear oil can be a temporary alternative, provided the chain is clean and you maintain it regularly. Avoid used engine oil or cooking oils, as they are ineffective and can harm your chain or the environment.
